receipt.public_excerpt: high benchmark accuracy does not reliably indicate visual understanding.

evidence_items.explanation: The study reports strong image-free benchmark performance and fabricated visual descriptions. Its published conclusion corroborates the broader warning that benchmark success can overstate visual understanding; the event date identifies the publication of this finding.

evidence_items.locator: Abstract, third sentence; authors and submission history
evidence_items.explanation: The named Nguyen-coauthored paper documents failures on simple visual tasks despite strong conventional benchmark performance. Its initial publication was July 2024; this quoted revision predates Marcus's post, and the human comparison is explicitly an expected accuracy.

This second Nguyen-coauthored paper shows prior knowledge and textual cues interfering with answers about altered images. It establishes an earlier related research finding, although its image-present experiments differ from MIRAGE's image-absent tests.

unresolved_gaps: No objective measure is supplied for whether the earlier papers were underappreciated; that description remains outside this empirical verdict.
